# ACC Magnetometer {.unnumbered #acc-magnetometer}

ACC means **antirelaxation coated cell**. The page is designed for weak-RF magnetometry calculations in which wall relaxation can be represented by the entered electron-randomization rate, while optical pumping and spin exchange prepare the atomic state.

## Atom and cell settings {#atom-and-cell-settings}

Alkali A is always active. Alkali B becomes active only when it is a different isotope or element from A. Enter the temperature, nitrogen pressure, electron-randomization rates, mixture density model, and static magnetic field.

The next sidebar row below electron randomization contains independent
uniform-relaxation rates $R_{u,A}$ and $R_{u,B}$, each defaulting to
$1\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$. These reset all ground-state populations toward equal
probabilities and damp every coherence, including nuclear polarization.
They affect the steady state, RF and optical response, physical-pump feedback,
and all total relaxation diagnostics. Use zero to disable this channel.

The field row contains polar angle $\theta$, azimuth $\phi$, and strength in nT.
Angles use integer degrees with 1° steps: $0\le\theta\le180$ measured from +z,
and $0\le\phi\le360$ from +x toward +y. A negative strength reverses the direction.
Thus $\mathbf B=B(\sin\theta\cos\phi,\sin\theta\sin\phi,\cos\theta)$.

The population model remains diagonal in the selected quantization basis.
Its Zeeman energies use the field component along that axis. For supported
secular RF response, choose parallel or antiparallel field and quantization
axes. Any nonzero transverse component disables the RF curve and shows a
warning, because coherent transverse mixing is outside this population model.

## Pump configuration {#pump-configuration}

Each species has up to three named pumps. A pump specifies:

- D1 or D2 spectral line;
- hyperfine reference transition and relative detuning;
- intensity in µW/cm²;
- propagation direction;
- polarization.

Every active optical frequency is evaluated against every active alkali species. A pump aimed at one species can therefore produce off-resonant pumping of another species, although reported target-specific light shifts follow the selected pump target.

## RF configuration {#rf-configuration}

RF-A drives and reads Alkali A; RF-B is defined conversely. The two species retain self- and cross-spin-exchange coupling even though only one RF source is applied for each displayed response.

Choose the RF axis, sweep bounds, and either a spin observable $F_i$ or the cyclic off-diagonal alignment observable $Q_{ij}$. The plotted curves are derivatives with respect to RF Rabi frequency or, for optical signals, may be converted to response per nT.

The same RF field drives both ground manifolds with their signed magnetic
couplings. **Hyperfine manifold** selects Fa ($F=I+1/2$), Fb ($F=I-1/2$), or
both overlaid; this changes only detection. New sessions show both. Atomic
responses are normalized to the common upper-manifold angular drive
$\Omega_a=g_a\mu_B B_{\mathrm{rf}}/\hbar$, using populations per total atom.
Optional relaxation normalization applies one common rate chosen at the largest
population difference across both manifolds. The transition table and colored
markers include both manifolds.

## Probe source modes {#probe-source-modes}

Every pump appears twice in the probe-source selector:

- `PumpN weak` copies the pump spectrum, direction, and polarization but ignores its intensity. It is a non-perturbing detector.
- `PumpN` selects the actual pump as the detected beam. Its configured intensity participates in the spatially uniform [physical-pump feedback model](../theory/uniform-density-matrix-feedback.qmd).
- `Custom Weak` defines an independent weak detector.

The physical-pump solver does **not** scale the configured intensity by the ratio of beam area to cell area.

## Results {#acc-results}

The results are divided into three sections:

1. Ground-state Zeeman properties and populations.
2. Atomic weak-RF response.
3. Optical response of the selected probe source.

A closed **Alkali A/B rate matrices** subsection is always available at the
end of the corresponding Zeeman section. Opening it displays
the optical generator, electron-randomization map, uniform-relaxation generator,
self/cross exchange maps and local population Jacobian. For two active species,
the coupled A/B population Jacobian is included at the end of this subsection.

Only open sections build their plots, tables and CSV downloads. Atomic and
optical response calculations are also deferred while their sections are closed.
Closing all physics result sections defers the equilibrium solve; pump-rate
captions in the sidebar still update from the optical models. Opening a section
uses the current conditions and reuses matching cached results.

Display controls update their own result section. RF axis and sweep bounds are
shared by the atomic and optical sections for that alkali. Weak-probe changes
reuse the equilibrium, and changing the atomic observable leaves optical
readout cached. Section open states and hidden display choices survive navigation;
Save includes committed choices made in individual result sections. Saved
condition schema 6.16 removes the former `show_rate_matrices` field; the
physics model is unchanged.

The former sidebar **Display** heading and **Show rate matrices** checkbox are
removed. A pinned bottom toolbar contains **Auto update** and **Apply**, matching
Time evolution. Auto update starts checked, with Apply disabled. Uncheck it to
batch atom/cell, pump or calculation-axis edits, then press Apply once. Pending
results and downloads are hidden until applied; sidebar pump-rate diagnostics
also wait. Applying with all physics sections closed still defers the equilibrium
solve until one is opened. RF/probe readout and display edits continue to reuse
the applied physical state. Auto update is an independent session preference;
it survives navigation and is not stored in condition files.

The optical panel can display fractional transmission, normalized Stokes parameters, rotation, or ellipticity. It can also display Total, Orientation induced, or Alignment induced responses. For physical-pump readout, the last two are separately closed counterfactual calculations and generally do not add to Total.

**Detected manifold** selects the optical contribution from Fa, Fb, or their
coherent Total. **Show manifold decomposition** overlays Fa and Fb. These
contributions add as complex signals, including for physical-pump readout,
where both are extracted from the same feedback closure. Their amplitudes do
not generally add. Rank decomposition remains an independent display choice.

Pump and probe F→F′ menus always list allowed hyperfine transitions. The
former checkbox and saved `show_allowed_only` field are removed. The selected
transition defines the detuning reference; all relevant allowed channels,
including off-resonant channels, still enter the calculations.

Condition files use schema **6.16**. Only this version is supported; older
files are rejected without migration. The two-manifold physics remains active.

See [Interpreting results](interpreting-results.qmd) for the phase convention and line-shape guidance.

Open response sections contribute their full content height to page scrolling.
The atomic and optical responses remain reachable together when the other
result sections are collapsed.
